advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the doubled remote-timeout (~60s) on the fetch+ls-remote outage path is acceptable, or bound the combined deadline.
evidence: _ref_lock.py:346-353: `result = _git(repo_root, ["fetch", ...], timeout=_REMOTE_TIMEOUT_SECS, ...)` then `_remote_ref_absent(...)` which itself runs `["ls-remote", "--exit-code", ...], timeout=_REMOTE_TIMEOUT_SECS`
ABSENCE: no shared/reduced deadline is threaded across the two remote calls, so their timeouts add on the outage path
advisory.finding: On an unreachable remote, a read with a stale local ref now performs two sequential remote-timeout-bounded git calls (fetch, then ls-remote), so a network-partitioned read can block up to ~2x _REMOTE_TIMEOUT_SECS (~60s) before returning fail-closed HELD, versus ~30s before.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either drop the redundant reclaimable test or restructure it to actually exercise steal-based recovery (e.g. a case where read() cannot prune).
evidence: test_lock_orphan_local_ref.py:148-155: `reads_free = ref_lock.read(...) is None` then `stolen = None if reads_free else ref_lock.steal(...)`
With the fix in _ref_lock.py:353-359, read() prunes the orphan so read() returns None -> reads_free True -> the steal(...) branch is dead code
test_preexisting_orphan_is_pruned_on_read already asserts the read()-prunes outcome, so this test's read-free branch is redundant and its steal branch never runs
advisory.finding: test_orphan_local_ref_is_reclaimable's steal() branch is unreachable given the shipped fix: read() now prunes the orphan and returns None, so `reads_free` is always True and steal() is never invoked, meaning the test no longer exercises the steal-based recovery path its docstring/message claims to cover.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with an unreachable/erroring remote (e.g. point `origin` at a nonexistent path or remove it) asserting a stranded local orphan is NOT pruned and `read()` still returns HELD (fail-closed).
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:353 `if _remote_ref_absent(repo_root, ref, remote) is True:` — prune ONLY on provable absence; the `is not True` (None) path leaves the local ref untouched and is the safety-critical direction of the fix

ABSENCE: all five tests build a real reachable bare remote via the `clone` fixture (tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_lock_orphan_local_ref.py:88-98); none simulate an unreachable/erroring remote (e.g. a bogus `origin` URL or removed remote), so the `_remote_ref_absent -> None` fail-closed branch is never executed. A regression pruning on `None` (or on any non-zero exit rather than exactly exit 2) would pass the whole suite.
advisory.finding: No test exercises the fail-closed unreachable-remote path (`_remote_ref_absent` returning `None`): when `git ls-remote` fails with a transport/auth error (exit != 0 and != 2), `_fetch_ref` must LEAVE the stranded local ref in place so a read still reports HELD, preserving cross-machine mutual exclusion during a network outage. The commit message claims this was verified ('an unreachable remote still reads HELD (fail-closed)'), but every test uses a reachable local bare remote.
scenarios: A refactor that treats any failed `ls-remote` as 'absent' (pruning the local ref during a network outage) — silently disabling cross-machine mutual exclusion — would not be caught.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `test_unreachable_remote_leaves_orphan_alone`: plant a local orphan (acquire+read), then break the remote (e.g. `git remote set-url origin /nonexistent` or delete the bare repo), and assert `ref_lock.read(clone, ref, remote='origin')` is not None and `_local_ref(clone, ref)` still equals the orphan oid.
